summary: In civil and international space developments, San Marino officially signed the NASA-led Artemis Accords to expand cooperative space exploration, while a private spacecraft re-entered Earth's atmosphere following a failed attempt to rescue an aging NASA telescope. In commercial industry trends, executive leadership at Rocket Lab forecasted an impending rise in sector-wide mergers and acquisitions. Scientific research yielded significant findings as the James Webb Space Telescope detected ammonia and an unexpected cold atmosphere on a distant giant planet, and astronomers reported that black hole jets extend far beyond the visible boundaries of their host galaxies. Defense and military developments were highlighted by South Korea inducting its first domestically developed fighter jet into operational service, while U.S. NORTHCOM strengthened strategic ties with Pacific and European commands to bolster Arctic security. Additionally, the U.S. Air Force certified Anduril’s Barracuda cruise missile for open system updates and allocated $87 million toward F-16 electronic warfare capabilities. Ahead of future orbital deployments, NASA completed testing on its Dual Mode Propulsion CubeSat. Readers should watch for an upcoming joint announcement from NASA and Boeing providing a status update on the development of the Starliner spacecraft.
